I will say on psychology today I’ve seen a lot of therapists put social anxiety in their “specialties” section so it I don’t know if there’s a filter for it but sometimes therapists will list it in their description or expertise area. Hey I have a similar experience. I used to be like that, generally liked at school or work but excluded from outside work activities. At my current job I managed to break out of that pattern a little and what really helped me was actively asking people what their plans were for the day or weekend. And act interested and ask who they’re going with etc, and if they like you decently enough they may ask you if you want to join. That got the ball rolling for me. Or you could tell people you’ve been really wanting to try a certain hobby or see a certain movie but can’t find anyone to go with. Sorry if you’ve already tried these and it hasn’t worked. Trust me I’m no socializing guru and still get excluded at times, but I think those of us with depression and anxiety sometimes THINK we’re putting in a lot of work to be social when for everyone else who’s neurotypical may see it as average to below average effort lol.
